correctness.rationale: Every endomorphism preserves the derived subgroup, which equals the center here. Its linear action A on the quotient scales the commutator form by det A, forcing that scalar on the center. After removing this scalar action, the central coordinate is an additive functional u; conversely the group law verifies all p^6 maps. Composition gives AB=BA and v(A−det(A)I)=u(B−det(B)I). Scalar A other than 0,I makes the latter map in v invertible and gives p^4 partners. For A=0,I, u=0 commutes universally, while nonzero u can be made (1,0), giving B=[[a,0],[c,d]] with a(1−d)=0 and p^2 free v, hence p^3(2p−1) partners. A nonscalar A has centralizer algebra span{I,A} by a cyclic-vector argument. When A−det(A)I is nonsingular this gives p^2 partners. Otherwise that matrix has rank one: its determinant vanishes precisely in the split distinct cases {0,t} with t≠0 or {1,t} with t≠0,1, or in a nonscalar Jordan case at 0 or 1. Ordered eigenspace lines count s=p(p+1)(2p−3) distinct-eigenvalue matrices; each nontrivial Jordan class has size p^2−1, giving j=2(p^2−1). The remaining nonscalar matrices number p^4−p−s−j. In the rank-one cases, u in the row space yields p choices of v for every B. For u outside, B=xI+yA must satisfy det B=x+y det A on the one-dimensional quotient. Its solution locus is two intersecting affine lines in the split case and two disjoint parallel lines in the Jordan case, yielding p(2p−1) and 2p^2 partners after counting v. The coefficients sum to p^6; the weighted sum simplifies to p^8+5p^7−8p^5+3p^3 and normalization by p^12 gives the ordered-pair probability. The seven centralizer sizes are strictly ordered for p≥3 and only 0 and the identity attain p^6. A separate exact matrix-and-functional census reproduced all seven multiplicities at p=3,5,7, with ordered-pair counts 15,633; 756,625; and 9,749,089 respectively.
residual_risks: The replay uses the derived coordinates and tests only p=3,5,7. The normal-form proof and case split, not the numerics, establish the theorem for all odd primes.

value.rationale: The smallest nonabelian exponent-p p-group is a natural first family for studying composition commutation beyond automorphism groups. The distribution identifies precisely which structural types and functionals create large centralizers and provides an exact all-odd-prime benchmark for higher-rank monoids. The commuting probability and monoid center are precise consequences not captured by the known endomorphism count or by group-element commuting probabilities.
residual_risks: No higher-rank, characteristic-two or exponent-p² monoid classification is claimed.
